title: Grandfather's Kampong
text:
My grandfather grew up in a kampong where the houses stood on wooden stilts and the chickens wandered wherever they pleased. There were no air-conditioners, he tells me, only the sea breeze and the shade of the rambutan trees.
When it rained, the children ran outside instead of indoors. When a family cooked something special, half the village smelled it and somehow half the village was invited. Doors were rarely locked, because everybody already knew everybody.
That kampong is gone now. In its place stand tall blocks of flats with lifts and covered walkways. My grandfather does not complain about the change. But sometimes, on quiet evenings, he looks out of the window for a long time, and I know exactly where he has gone.
